decision: Hold release. No third-party source transformations proposed for promotion.
shippingTarget: Windows x86_64, MO2 Python plugin and WebView2 desktop
independence: A separate reviewer reran shrink and static Rust analysis on the candidate source export. The DOM capture, benchmark and two matching modules were byte-identical between the two reviewed commits. Existing native A/B data was reviewed separately.

inspection: Verified immutable release tags and GitHub release-archive SHA-256 before extracting executable members. Checked license files and Cargo manifests and locks.

Inspected runtime entry points, npm platform wrappers and publish/install scripts. Release publishing, coding-agent invocation, file-cutting, local MCP registration, Rust port generation and activation run outside the review scope. Rust doctor starts its own transient stdio MCP diagnostic in the guest.

Queried OSV querybatch by exact public crates.io name/version for each locked registry package and the public GitHub security-advisory endpoint for each upstream repository. Counts are observations on the review date.
supplyChain.execution: Verified Windows binaries ran in a capability-free Windows AppContainer with synthetic input and fresh local homes. Tests confirmed denial of outbound TCP and an external sentinel. Windows denied child NUL access and path canonicalization for profiling. Unmodified upstream Linux binaries subsequently profiled the same fixture in a non-root, RAM-only guest inside the AppContainer, with no emulated NIC, disks or host shares. The guest had a private home and no production credentials. The emulator, runtimes and caches were confined to the review directory.

baseline.sourceMode: Immutable Git source export. MO2 library inventory was read separately using the product executable. Third-party tools received only product source, build artifacts and synthetic matching rows.

testInventory.scope: Discovery checks imports and inventory. Execution, difference coverage and shipped workflows are separate release checks.

compatibilitySurface: MO2 host-discovered Python entry point, Qt signals and public callables
Rust CLI/MCP command dispatch and serialization
WebView2 content extraction, CSP, negotiated capabilities and dynamic registration
Linked assets, translations, archived installers, saves, prior-version data and release evidence

shrink.decision: Retain both public symbols, the Windows path validation, and separately linked assets. Reference counts alone do not cover public MO2 and Rust callers. Tracked source archives are distinct release deliverables. No cut, dependency removal, deduplication or package-size reduction was accepted.

workload.reproduction: Copy the fixture to the root of a disposable candidate source tree under its basename, keeping mo2_update_arsenal importable. Run the profiler commands below from there.
workload.input: 11,325 generated rows, repeated three times, with a prior file, a current file and an inconsistent same-file version in equal proportions. The product file-index and version comparison functions run on every row.
workload.normalizedOutput: Ordered position/verdict/target-ID lines encoded as UTF-8.
workload.limitations: Known-answer arithmetic and the row digest cover fixture verdicts, order and target IDs. Live I/O, UI, metadata variance and provider latency require separate coverage.

commands.reason: AppContainer denied the runtime detection subprocess.
Windows denied the child NUL handle.
Python ready to scan. Deliberately absent Cargo blocks port compilation.

rankedFindings: The first proposed port was the fixture loop; it does not ship.
compare_versions had 33,975 calls and 59.2% inclusive time. NexusFileIndex.compare had 33,975 calls and 65.3% inclusive time. Nested percentages overlap.
fast.decision: No port selected. Sampling shows the local comparison routines execute frequently, but the end-to-end workflow includes provider and MO2 costs, and the hot fixture loop is test-only. A native extension would add a Windows packaging and ABI obligation.

commands.reason: The sandbox and absent Rust toolchain restrict diagnostics.
Cargo unavailable. The temporary stdio MCP self-test advertised 22 tools.

rust.decision: The independent run suggests the same comparison family as Fast. Complete Windows cProfile observed 0.799 s cumulative for resolve and 0.500 s for compare_versions across 33,975 rows in this fixture. Neither a native port nor a bridge-inclusive speedup was established. No recording, scaffolding or rewrite was selected.

nativeImport.scope: Complete native import of a real selected MO2 profile
nativeImport.runs: Two processes per build, 12 warm runs each. Alternate build order. Filesystem caching and concurrent large-volume hashing influenced the measurements.
nativeImport.decision: The measured change moves owned JSON values inside the existing Rust importer. The complete catalog and warnings compared equal. It avoids another language boundary. Fresh final-build results are required before ascribing these figures to a shipped package.

browserExtraction.decision: Both paths matched every expected byte in every run. The ignore-selector branch improved materially. The empty-selector control was effectively unchanged. Timing covers completed in-page extraction, excluding WebView2, network, browser startup and host IPC.

remainingReleaseGates: Verify the final promotion SHA and package digests after all subsequent changes. Re-run complete test execution and original test-inventory/coverage parity on the final package.

The Athena governance adoption snapshot is an independent known failing baseline in current repository history. Preserve owner pins and the original test; resolve or obtain the owner decision before claiming the gate passed.

Confirm Windows MO2/plugin discovery, actual WebView2 workflows, portable packaging, data/save restoration, install/reinstall/cancellation and offline behavior on the final binary. Keep the production profile protected.

Recheck exact final native builds, clippy/fmt/test, applicable dependency and license advisories, ABI compatibility, complete outputs, and cold/warm resource tails including startup and bridge costs. Validate a material change beyond noise for future ports.
rollback: No third-party cut or port changed product code. The native import change and DOM change remain individually versioned and reviewable. Restore their respective commits in a disposable checkout and rerun equal-output benchmarks for a fallback comparison.
